Winter clusters form, with bees rotating positions from periphery to center, balancing survival with energy expenditure. Research shows that even minor hive imbalances trigger coordinated responses, revealing a distributed problem-solving system. This social homeostasis is remarkable considering that each bee has only millimeters of sensory perception, yet collectively they maintain a climate comparable to modern technology. Historical beekeepers noted winter die-offs when colonies failed at thermoregulation, highlighting the life-or-death importance of this behavior. Evolution has produced a tiny cooperative workforce capable of continuous environmental control without central planning. The hive operates as a single organism in terms of thermal intelligence.
